artifacts.researchQuestion: Resolve the reproducible customer-concentration portion of the active gating gap from current primary filings; keep future export-policy path separate as a documented unknown.
artifacts.summary: Current SEC filings provide a reproducible concentration series sufficient for Chief to review the customer-concentration gate without guessing customer identities. FY2026 had two direct customers at 22% and 14% of revenue; Q2 FY2027 had one direct customer at 16%, while H1 FY2027 had three direct customers at 16%, 15%, and 13%. Accounts receivable concentration at July 26, 2026 was 22%, 14%, 13%, 11%, and 10% across five direct customers. NVIDIA explicitly says revenue remains concentrated among limited direct and indirect customers.
evidence: FY2026 Form 10-K: two direct customers represented 22% and 14% of total revenue, primarily Compute & Networking.
Q2 FY2027 Form 10-Q: one direct customer represented 16% of quarterly revenue; H1 FY2027 three direct customers represented 16%, 15%, and 13%.
Q2 FY2027 balance-sheet note: five direct customers represented 22%, 14%, 13%, 11%, and 10% of accounts receivable at July 26, 2026.
artifacts.inference: The concentration risk is material and directly measurable even though customer names are not disclosed. Exact customer identity is not necessary to preserve a conservative concentration treatment; do not fabricate identities from channel speculation.
unknowns: Exact identities of disclosed direct customers remain undisclosed in the cited filings.
Future export-policy path remains unknown and should not be converted into a current company-promotion blocker unless the locked methodology explicitly requires a resolved future policy outcome.
The separate active gate for normalized capital-return/dilution treatment is not resolved by this artifact.
falsifiers: A later primary filing showing no direct customer at or above 10% of revenue and materially lower receivable concentration would weaken the current concentration-risk treatment.
A methodology contract requiring named customer identities rather than issuer-disclosed concentration percentages would require a different source path.

artifacts.researchQuestion: Reconcile current cash runway, dilution channels and acquisition accounting from the latest primary filing, separating current gating facts from Neutron timing uncertainty.
artifacts.summary: The June 30, 2026 10-Q materially closes the cash/dilution/acquisition-accounting fact gap. Rocket Lab reported $2.129 billion cash plus $258.105 million current/non-current marketable securities ($2.388 billion combined), stated those resources plus customer payments are sufficient for at least the next 12 months, and disclosed $37.6 million principal of convertible notes outstanding. Dilution is observable: 4,858,839 ATM shares were issued for about $90.1 million net proceeds in the reported equity roll-forward, 3,502,374 shares were issued under equity plans in the same roll-forward section, and 19,315,464 ESPP shares remained available for issuance. Six-month SBC was $47.677 million, including an $11.180 million one-time charge from cancellation of 392,155 CEO RSUs that will not dilute shareholders. Mynaric consideration was primarily 2,277,002 Rocket Lab shares, with $99.073 million identifiable intangibles and $60.006 million goodwill; acquired operations contributed $13.195 million revenue and $13.245 million operating loss in the quarter.
evidence: June 30, 2026 cash and equivalents: $2.129485 billion; current marketable securities $172.700 million; non-current marketable securities $85.405 million; total $2.387590 billion.
Issuer states existing cash/securities and customer payments are sufficient for working capital and capex for at least 12 months, while preserving optional opportunistic financing.
$37.6 million aggregate principal of convertible senior notes remained outstanding as of March 31, 2026 per the 2026 filing sequence.
Equity roll-forward discloses 4,858,839 ATM shares for approximately $90.103 million net proceeds and 3,502,374 shares issued under equity plans.
Six-month SBC was $47.677 million; CEO cancellation removed 392,155 unvested RSUs from future dilution, despite an $11.180 million one-time accounting charge.
Mynaric acquisition used 2,277,002 common shares; preliminary allocation included $99.073 million intangibles and $60.006 million goodwill.
artifacts.inference: Near-term liquidity is not the unresolved gating problem on the latest filing. The remaining Chief review should normalize recurring SBC/equity issuance and acquisition-related dilution/accounting rather than treating runway as unknown. Neutron schedule uncertainty remains a separate non-gating future uncertainty under the queue's own classification.
contradictions: The issuer says at least 12 months of liquidity is sufficient but also explicitly reserves opportunistic capital raising/refinancing; this is not a contradiction, but it means 'sufficient runway' must not be interpreted as 'no future dilution.'
unknowns: Exact future dilution from unvested awards and future ATM use remains contingent and should not be fabricated.

The announced Iridium transaction after quarter-end introduces a much larger prospective financing/capital-structure question; its closing financing should be evaluated from definitive transaction/financing filings before treating the current June balance sheet as post-deal liquidity.
Neutron timing remains non_gating_unknown unless methodology explicitly requires a resolved launch date.
falsifiers: A subsequent financing or definitive Iridium funding filing that materially changes cash, debt or share count would supersede the June 30 normalization.
A later amended acquisition allocation could change goodwill/intangible normalization.

artifacts.researchQuestion: Resolve the active current capex/debt normalization gate using the latest primary quarterly filing while preserving HBM scarcity duration as non-gating future uncertainty.
artifacts.summary: Micron's Q3 FY2026 10-Q provides a clean current normalization: approximately $27 billion FY2026 net capex guidance; $19.60 billion PP&E spend in the first nine months, partially offset by $2.99 billion government-incentive proceeds; $5.72 billion carrying-value debt; $2.00 billion undrawn revolver capacity; and $25.022 billion ending cash/cash-equivalents/restricted cash, with $30.128 billion total fair value across cash, short-term investments and long-term marketable investments in the disclosed investment table. Nine-month operating cash flow was $45.702 billion versus $19.688 billion net investing cash use. This supports a reproducible capital-intensity/debt/liquidity treatment without making a forecast about HBM scarcity duration.
evidence: FY2026 PP&E capex net of government incentives is estimated at approximately $27 billion.
First nine months FY2026 PP&E expenditures were $19.60 billion, partially offset by $2.99 billion government incentives.
Debt carrying value was $5.72 billion at May 28, 2026; $2.00 billion remained available under the revolving credit facility.
Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash ended at $25.022 billion; disclosed cash/investment fair value totaled $30.128 billion.
Nine-month operating cash flow was $45.702 billion and net investing cash use was $19.688 billion.
artifacts.inference: The current capex/debt normalization gate is sufficiently evidenced for Chief scoring review: Micron is highly capital intensive but presently has substantial internally generated cash and liquidity relative to debt. The treatment should retain capex intensity and incentive/clawback dependency rather than converting strong current cash flow into a low-capital-intensity conclusion.
unknowns: HBM scarcity duration and future memory-cycle pricing remain non_gating_unknown and should not hold current promotion.
Future government incentive realization is conditional and subject to compliance/clawback; do not net unearned future incentives into current liquidity.
falsifiers: A later filing with materially higher debt, lower liquidity, reduced operating cash generation or sharply higher capex would require renormalization.
Failure to satisfy government-incentive conditions would weaken the net-capex economics.
